dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Hello there. So this is where you live...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Mind if I take a quick stroll around? You know me — I like to keep moving.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I like it a lot. The air here is crisp and fresh, which is good for both body and mind.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Although, I didn't see a dedicated training area... Want me to help you set up a gym? I can plan it out and get the equipment for you.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Alright, then I have some thinking to do.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: First, we should tackle the equipment, and this is where it's important to take a lot of care. You wouldn't believe how many injuries start with poor equipment choice.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Oh, how about this? Give me some time, and I'll ask a friend to make you a custom set.

choices.text: Eh, adventuring keeps me in good enough shape.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Very fair... Everyone has different approaches to physical fitness.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Some people prefer the great outdoors to a gym. For a traveler like you, hiking and running from place to place are great kinds of exercise.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's wrong? Are you worried about something?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Ah... Sorry. I was just thinking about the curriculum for my next batch of students.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Curriculum?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Yeah, their training curriculum.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Physical fitness is big thing in the Collective of Plenty. As the head coach of Fitness Club, I'm in charge of the newcomers.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You can't just reuse the curriculum from previous years?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Ah, you think the same exercises work for everyone? That's what most people think when they start out.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Let me ask you this... What do you think is the most important thing when it comes to fitness?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Let's use that as an example, then. A lot of people think all exercises are created equal — as long as you're doing something to keep active, you'll achieve your fitness goals.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: But in reality, everyone starts from a different baseline. So, I design regimens that account for different circumstances.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: If a student is on the heavier side, I usually ease them into cardio exercises like running to lower their body weight.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: If a student is very lean, I usually start them off with resistance training to build muscle.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Lumping everyone into the same regimen is just asking for injuries.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: As a result, a new batch of students means designing tailored curriculum to meet their needs.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wow, being a fitness coach sounds like a lot of work...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Well, when you like what you do, it's not work at all!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: My Ancient Name means "strength." So, it feels really connected to my profession. Training is a means to gain strength, but you only get out what you put in. There are no shortcuts.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: With every student I teach, I gain a deeper understanding of my Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: By the way, do you have any fitness goals of your own? I can craft a training plan for you.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: But, fitness is a journey, not a destination. You have a great foundation, which is never a bad thing, but don't get complacent, or it might not stay that way!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Haha, welcome to the club. As far as the training plan goes... let's start with the nutrition side of things. It's the biggest hurdle for a lot of my students.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Now, that's a whole other can of worms. But, at the most basic level, nutrition plans need to be tailored from student to student, as well.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: For some students, it's about gaining weight — eating enough calories to keep up with the physical demands of training. That's something I always try to impart on my students — the number on the scale is not a measure of fitness.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: For those who are at a good fitness level, it's all about balance. A lack of diligence about what you put in your body is a sure fire way to ruin all your progress.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: So, I usually design customized nutrition plans for every student.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anything you want to do?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I like to meditate sometimes! I learned it from the Masters of the Night-Wind. It's a nice mental work-out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is that considered a part of fitness training, too?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Hmm... The best answer to that... is a story.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Many, many years ago, there lived a great warrior in the Collective of Plenty. He loved to train, and loved showing off his strength even more.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: He started with weightlifting competitions. Then, he progressed to wrestling tatankasaurs, and finally, he challenged a Long-Necked Rhino.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: To everyone's surprise, he bested every challenge.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: People recognized him as the strongest warrior in Natlan, but he still wasn't satisfied. So, he came up with a crazy plan.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Pushing a giant boulder up the sacred volcano and using it to seal off the crater... proving him capable of besting the might of Tollan in the process.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: He stopped at nothing to accomplish his goal, including ingesting dangerous medications.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Finally, he made an attempt, and began pushing a mountain-sized boulder up the slope of the volcano.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: But, just as he made it half-way, the volcano erupted. He lost his footing, and the boulder fell and crushed him to death.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Ironically, only a boulder of such enormous size could have bested him. Similarly, only a man of his strength could have placed himself in such a precarious position.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: In the end, it was his own desire to prove his strength that led to his downfall.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wow, I never knew...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: So, training isn't just about getting stronger. It's about control and discipline.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: That's why the mental side of training is so important. It means you're not a slave to your own power.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like you're a master in that area, too.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: ...Actually, compared to the newcomers, it's harder for me to keep that desire in check sometimes.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: There was a time when I really liked pushing my limits. I always wanted to do that one extra push-up or bench press, and every time I got a personal best, I was ecstatic...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Now that I look back on it, I feel like that was my own boulder and volcano.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: So, as a friend, I have a favor to ask — if I ever succumb to that mindless drive again, pull me back, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I know you have what it takes.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You have my word.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Thank you. Then, let's close our eyes and meditate together. Oh, and don't try and fake it, okay? I can always tell.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Iansan.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Morning! Don't forget to eat breakfast — it's important for maintaining nutritional balance throughout the day.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Iansan.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Good night. Going to bed early is a good habit to get into. That way, you can start your day off early as well!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Thank you for installing all this furniture. It makes me feel like I'm right back home. Although, it'll still take me some time to adjust to not having the view of the Sacred Mountain on the other side of the roof...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Come visit me at the Collective of Plenty sometime. I'll be your host.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Sure, it's good to have a cozy place to call home, but there's more to life than being cozy. The real meaning is in the journey.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Now that I think about it, blacksmithing is a great workout.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I've visited Xilonen's workshop a bunch of times whenever I need to commission some custom equipment... Always wanted to try my hand at hammering something, but she never let me.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: But since you have a whole setup here... Would it be alright if I used it? That way, I can try out any new ideas I have as soon as they pop into my head.
